newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico peso firmer on U.S. long bond, futures.
newsitem.headline: Mexico peso firmer on U.S. long bond, futures.

text.p: The Mexixcan peso opened firmer across the board on Thursday as a firm U.S. long bond and peso futures trading in Chicago encouraged dealers to shed long dollar positions, dealers said.
"I think the peso could have another good day, the market won't want to be caught napping with long dollars, especially with the peso getting stronger, " a trader said.
The benchmark 48-hour peso and its 24-hour counterpart opened 1.75 and 2.1 centavos firmer, respectively, at 7.8560/7.8625 and 7.8500/7.8540 per dollar.
Same-day peso contracts had meanwhile opened trade 7.5 centavos firmer at 7.8450/7.8500 per dollar in order to line up with late strength by longer contracts during the prior session.
The U.S. 30-year Treasury bond stood unchanged and yielding 6.48 percent.
Traders said brokers could also be switching to the money market ahead of the weekend.
Early bids on overnight Cetes rates were down 40 basis points at 19.10 percent.
Dealers forecast the 48-hour peso could trade at between 7.8500/7.8800 per dollar.
